title: Canonical quasi-coherent sheaf identification on an open
statement: Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-open-immersion] and let $F$ be a quasi-coherent module on $X$ [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $F_{\mathrm{et}}(v:V\to X)=\Gamma(V,v^*F)$ with the normalized pullback section restrictions [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module, lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial]. Restrict this sheaf by precomposition with $U_{\mathrm{Et}}\to X_{\mathrm{Et}}$, $v\mapsto j\circ v$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. There is an isomorphism from this restricted abelian sheaf to $(F|_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$. Its component at every $v:V\to U$ is $\Gamma(V,c_{v,j}^{-1})$ followed by $\Gamma(V,v^*\kappa_F^{-1})$, where $c_{v,j}$ is normalized pullback composition [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition, lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] and $\kappa_F:F|_U\cong j^*F$ is the canonical open restriction comparison [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction]. The formula determines the sheaf isomorphism and uses natural module-functor isomorphisms, hence is natural in $F$.

proof.text: Construct each component explicitly by evaluating inverse normalized pullback composition followed by pullback of the canonical tensor/restriction comparison. Functor.mapIso proves each is invertible. The section naturality equation gives NatIso.ofComponents; ObjectProperty.isoMk lifts it between the two sheaves without sheafification. Its hom components are the prescribed formula by reflexivity.
